cls: Dental caries prophylactic agent - fluoride supplement / topical anticaries
pharm: Fluoride ion is incorporated into developing and surface tooth enamel, converting hydroxyapatite to acid-resistant fluorapatite, promotes remineralization of early carious lesions, and inhibits bacterial enzymes/acid production, thereby reducing dental caries.
quick: Topical rinse 0.05% NaF (10 mL) once daily; supplements mainly for children
Avoid eating/drinking/rinsing for ~30 min after topical use; supplements may be given on empty stomach
Prenatal fluoride not recommended for fetal benefit; routine maternal use as usual
Compatible; little fluoride passes into milk
Caution in significant renal impairment (reduced fluoride excretion)
Avoid swallowing alcohol-containing rinses; otherwise no specific interaction
Dental status, signs of dental/skeletal fluorosis, water-fluoride content
summary: Sodium fluoride is used to prevent dental caries. Systemic fluoride supplements (tablets, lozenges, drops) are prescribed for children living in areas with inadequately fluoridated drinking water, with the dose carefully scaled to the child's age and the fluoride concentration of the local water supply; no supplement is given when water fluoride is adequate. Topical preparations (rinses, gels, dentifrices) deliver fluoride directly to erupted teeth to strengthen enamel and promote remineralization. Fluoride works by forming acid-resistant fluorapatite, enhancing remineralization of early lesions, and inhibiting cariogenic bacteria. The principal safety concern is excessive intake: chronic overexposure causes dental fluorosis (enamel mottling) and, at high cumulative doses, skeletal fluorosis, while large acute ingestions are toxic. Doses must be individualized and total fluoride intake from all sources considered.
indications: Prevention of dental caries in children in areas where the drinking-water fluoride concentration is suboptimal (systemic supplementation)
Topical strengthening of enamel and prevention of caries in children and adults (rinses, gels, varnishes, dentifrices)
Reduction of dentinal hypersensitivity (certain topical formulations)

dosage.c: Supplement - water F <0.3 ppm, age 6 months-3 years
dosage.n: Per ADA/AAP fluoride supplement schedule; no supplement before 6 months

dosage.c: Supplement - water F <0.3 ppm, age 3-6 years
Supplement - water F <0.3 ppm, age 6-16 years

dosage.d: Half the above dose for each age band; none if <3 years; 0.25 mg (3-6 yr); 0.50 mg (6-16 yr)
dosage.n: No supplement if water F >0.6 ppm

dosage.d: 0.05% sodium fluoride solution, 10 mL swished for 1 minute then expectorated, once daily
dosage.n: Do not swallow; for ages >=6 years

dosage.d: 0.2% sodium fluoride solution rinse once weekly

admin: Determine the fluoride concentration of the child's drinking water BEFORE prescribing a systemic supplement; do not give if water fluoride is adequate (>0.6 ppm)
Give oral fluoride supplements with little food/milk if maximal absorption is desired, or chew tablets/let lozenges dissolve near the teeth for added topical benefit
For rinses: swish the measured volume for the stated time, then spit out - do not swallow; avoid eating, drinking, or rinsing for ~30 minutes
Keep all fluoride products out of reach of children - acute ingestion can be toxic
Account for total fluoride from water, toothpaste, foods, and supplements to avoid excess (fluorosis)
moa: Fluoride exerts its anticaries effect by three main mechanisms. When present during tooth formation it is incorporated systemically into developing enamel, converting hydroxyapatite to fluorapatite, which is more resistant to acid dissolution. Topically and post-eruptively, fluoride in saliva and plaque promotes remineralization of early (incipient) carious lesions and is taken up into the surface enamel as it remineralizes. Fluoride also inhibits bacterial enzymes (such as enolase) in cariogenic plaque organisms, reducing their acid production. Together these effects lower the rate of demineralization, enhance remineralization, and reduce dental caries.

absolute: Areas where the drinking-water fluoride content is already optimal or high (systemic supplements not indicated)
relative: Young children unable to control swallowing (avoid concentrated rinses/gels)
monitor: Dental examination for caries and signs of fluorosis (enamel mottling)
Total fluoride intake from all sources
Signs of skeletal fluorosis with long-term high exposure

preg: Routine prenatal fluoride supplementation for the benefit of the fetus is not recommended, as evidence of caries benefit to the offspring is lacking. Maternal fluoride from normal water and dental products is acceptable. Avoid excessive total intake.
lact: Fluoride is considered compatible with breastfeeding; only small amounts are transferred into breast milk regardless of maternal intake, so the breastfed infant's fluoride exposure from milk is low.
renal: Fluoride is eliminated by the kidneys. In significant renal impairment, fluoride excretion is reduced and may accumulate; use supplements cautiously and consider lower exposure to avoid fluorosis or toxicity.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Calcium, magnesium, aluminum (dairy products, antacids, some supplements) - form poorly absorbed complexes that reduce fluoride absorption; separate administration
Iron supplements - may reduce fluoride absorption
minor: High-dose fluoride may interact with absorption of certain minerals
interactions.food: Milk and other calcium- or magnesium-rich foods/antacids reduce fluoride absorption; for systemic effect separate from dairy.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid swallowing alcohol-containing fluoride rinses; otherwise no specific interaction.
interactions.diagnostics: Chronic excess may show characteristic enamel mottling (dental fluorosis) and increased bone density on imaging (skeletal fluorosis).

common: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses
serious: Dental fluorosis (enamel mottling/staining) from chronic excess during tooth development
Skeletal fluorosis (bone pain, stiffness) from prolonged high intake
Acute fluoride toxicity from large ingestion
emergency: Acute fluoride poisoning - nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, salivation, tetany, cardiac arrhythmia from hypocalcemia (large ingestion)

monitoring: Periodic dental examination for caries and enamel fluorosis
Assessment of total fluoride intake from water, toothpaste, food, and supplements
Verification of local water fluoride level before/while supplementing
Signs of skeletal fluorosis in long-term high exposure
counsel: Take or apply exactly as prescribed - more fluoride is not better and can stain or damage developing teeth
If using a mouth rinse, swish and then spit it out; do not swallow it, and do not eat or drink for about 30 minutes afterward
Keep fluoride tablets, drops, and rinses out of children's reach - swallowing a large amount is dangerous
Tell your dentist your drinking-water source so the right dose can be chosen for your child
Use a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste for young children and supervise brushing to limit swallowing
Avoid taking fluoride supplements at the same time as milk or dairy, which reduce absorption
pk: Topical effect immediate on enamel; caries benefit over months-years
Plasma fluoride peaks ~30-60 minutes after ingestion
Plasma half-life ~2-9 hours; long retention in bone/teeth
Once-daily or weekly dosing maintains protective levels
Store at controlled room temperature; keep out of reach of children
pearls: Dental dosing is individualized by the child's AGE and the local drinking-water fluoride level - no supplement if water fluoride is adequate (>0.6 ppm)
No systemic fluoride supplement before 6 months of age
Chronic excess during enamel formation causes dental fluorosis (mottling); long-term high intake causes skeletal fluorosis
Acute large ingestion is toxic (GI symptoms, hypocalcemia, arrhythmia) - keep away from children, treat with calcium/milk and supportive care
Topical fluoride (toothpaste, rinse, varnish) is the mainstay of caries prevention; supplements are adjunctive where water is under-fluoridated
Separate from milk/antacids/iron, which reduce absorption of systemic fluoride
missed: If you miss a dose of a fluoride supplement or rinse, take or use it when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. Consistent daily use over time is what protects the teeth.
overdose: Acute fluoride ingestion can cause nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, excessive salivation, and, with large amounts, hypocalcemia leading to tetany, cardiac arrhythmias, and CNS depression. Give milk, calcium- or magnesium-containing antacids, or calcium gluconate to bind fluoride; provide fluids, correct hypocalcemia, and give supportive/intensive care for large ingestions. Seek emergency care or poison control immediately.
